[Guide index](start-here.html) | Guide 3 of 5

This guide is standalone and uses invented records. A window joins a person's
records to a specific entry's dates. It does not flag disease or decide eligibility.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## 1. Identify the source and entries

```{r data}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)
visits <- data.frame(
  patient = c("A", "A", "A", "B"),
  visit_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-10", "2020-01-11", "2020-01-10")),
  diagnosis = c("J06", "K35", "E11", "J06")
)
entries <- data.frame(
  pid = c("A", "A", "C"),
  entry_id = c("A-first", "A-second", "C-first"),
  index_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-10", "2020-01-11", "2020-01-10"))
)
```

One person can have several entries, but `entry_id` must uniquely identify each
entry. Here source `patient` and cohort `pid` have different names; the mapping
is explicitly **source name = cohort name**. Keys must have compatible types.

## 2. Plan a relative window, then collect

```{r relative}
plan <- thip_window(
  visits, entries,
  by = c(patient = "pid"), entry = "entry_id",
  date = "visit_date", index = "index_date", window = c(-9L, 1L)
)
plan
records <- collect(plan, batch_size = 1L)
records
```

`date` names the source record date; `index` names the cohort reference date.
Both must be R `Date` values (or a supported SQL date source), not timestamps.
The default `[)` includes the lower boundary and excludes the upper one. For
A-first, 1–10 January match; 11 January does not. A record may match both of A's
windows. Original source columns remain unchanged; the result adds `entry_id`.
Duplicates in the source are preserved, not silently deduplicated.

`window` means integer day offsets, not calendar months/years. Other bounds are
`[]`, `(]`, and `()`. Missing source IDs/dates do not match. Invalid cohort
IDs/dates raise an error.

## 3. Use explicit dates for study-end follow-up

```{r explicit}
followup_entries <- entries |>
  mutate(start_date = index_date, end_date = as.Date("2020-02-01"))
followup <- thip_window(
  visits, followup_entries, by = c(patient = "pid"), date = "visit_date",
  start = "start_date", end = "end_date"
) |>
  collect()
followup
```

Use either explicit `start`/`end` columns or relative `index`/`window` arguments.
An end date can be years later; annual extraction must not break person timelines.

## 4. Keep entries with no matching records

```{r roster}
matched <- records |> count(entry_id, name = "matched_rows")
roster <- entries |>
  left_join(matched, by = "entry_id") |>
  mutate(matched_rows = coalesce(matched_rows, 0L))
roster
```

C has no source records but stays in the entry roster. Zero matches do not prove
no disease or adequate observation. These are **matched row counts**, not distinct
admission counts. Overlap and source duplicates matter if you count encounters.

## Remote execution and batching

With a lazy THIP source, the connection is inherited from that source. Apply
ordinary `select()` and `filter()` **before** `thip_window()`: the resulting plan
is not a general dbplyr table. Printing a plan does not fetch rows; `collect()`
executes it. No temporary DB tables are created.

`batch_size` counts distinct people, keeping all windows for one person together.
It is not a row limit. Changing it does not change match semantics. All returned
rows still occupy R memory; this is not disk streaming. Oversized SQL batches
fail with guidance to reduce the batch size; failed queries do not return a
partial successful result. For diagnostics, inspect `attr(records, "window_report")`.
